title: The smoothing bridge: the weight defect and the smoothing law at the critical line
summary: Replacing the sharp cutoff in a Dirichlet partial sum by a smooth weight is the standard way to suppress truncation fluctuation. Can smoothing extract zeta(1/2+it) to o(1), even exponentially small, accuracy so a finite-N condition sees a zeta zero? Answer: no. Proved in Lean 4 (no sorry, no new axiom): the weight defect identity, its triangle bound, radial decay, the sigma>1 summability comparison and quadratic-weight closed forms. Proved on paper and verified to 5-7 digits: |S_N^phi(1/2+it)-zeta(1/2+it)|/sqrt(N) -> |M_phi(s)|, so every weight keeps the sqrt(N) growth and smoothing buys only a constant. Refuted: the draft constant 1/sqrt(2t).
